newsitem.title: USA: CIA officer held on charges of spying for Moscow.
newsitem.headline: CIA officer held on charges of spying for Moscow.

text.p: A CIA officer has been arrested on charges that he spied for Moscow, law enforcement officials said on Monday.
The suspect, whose identity was not immediately released, was to appear before a federal magistrate at 11 a.m. (1600 GMT) in Alexandria, Virginia, the officials said.

They said the director of central intelligence, John Deutch, and the director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Louis Freeh, were planning to hold a joint press conference at 1 p.m. (1800 GMT) at FBI headquarters to discuss the arrest.

The CIA and the FBI have been hunting for another possible CIA turncoat since the Feb. 21, 1994, arrest of Aldrich Ames, who is serving a life prison term for selling secrets to Moscow over a 10-year period.
The New York Times reported on Monday that the arrested CIA employee was an instructor who trained other agency officials and had been stationed overseas.
He was reportedly arrested on Saturday in Virginia after a lengthy investigation.
The suspect's espionage work began as early as 1994, and possibly as far back as 1991 before the collapse of the Soviet Union and communism in Eastern Europe, the Times reported.
The suspect reportedly had access to secret material on a wide range of issues involving Russia and the former Soviet Union's Cold War satellite states.
